en: Arriving in Xi'an: Airport, Stations and Transfers
zh: 抵达西安：机场、车站与市内换乘
ja: 西安に着く：空港、駅、市内の乗り換え

p.src: Before following the crowd to the first escalator, read the station name on the ticket carefully: Xi'an North, Xi'an Station or Xi'an East. At the airport, identify T5, T2 or T3, then open the hotel's Chinese address. The four guides pause outside the station to settle only three things: the exact hub, the next mode, and the final hotel entrance. Do not treat similar station names or separate terminals as the same place.

caption.zh: 西安北站前，四位向导把行李收在身边，先核对车站、下一段交通和酒店入口，再进入换乘。宽阔站前空间不等于只有一个出口或乘车区。
caption.ja: 西安北駅前で、四人は荷物を手元にまとめ、駅名、次の交通手段、ホテル入口を確認してから乗り換えへ進む。広い駅前空間にも出口と乗車場所は複数ある。
caption.en: Outside Xi'an North, the four guides keep their luggage together and confirm the station, next mode and hotel entrance before transferring. A broad forecourt does not mean there is only one exit or pickup zone.

p.src: The map keeps only the links that change the first transfer. Line 14 joins the airport to Xi'an North, where Lines 2 and 4 offer different routes into the city. Xi'an Station sits north of the wall on Line 4; Xi'an East has a walking connection to Line 5. The lines are schematic: they show neither the full metro network nor travel times. Identify the hub here, then use the current official network and live navigation for the route to the hotel entrance.

caption.zh: 机场、西安北站、西安站与西安东站的第一次换乘判断。彩色线只保留14、2、4、5号线中会改变进城方向的部分，不是完整地铁图、车程或实时导航。
caption.ja: 空港、西安北駅、西安駅、西安東駅からの最初の乗り換え判断。色線は十四・二・四・五号線のうち進行方向を決める部分だけを示し、地下鉄全図、所要時間、当日のナビではない。
caption.en: First-transfer decisions from the airport, Xi'an North, Xi'an Station and Xi'an East. The coloured spines retain only the parts of Lines 14, 2, 4 and 5 that change the cityward choice; they are not the complete metro, journey times or live navigation.

p.src: The airport no longer fits the old T1-T2-T3 description. T5 opened in February 2025 and currently handles all international, Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan services as well as selected domestic airlines. From T5 arrivals, follow signs into the integrated transport centre for the station named Airport (T5). T2 and T3 use Airport West (T1, T2, T3) and have separate paths to taxis and airport buses. Airline assignments can move, so trust the boarding pass, current flight information and airport display rather than memory.

p.src: When Line 14 reaches Xi'an North from the airport, stop and reconsider the route rather than transferring automatically to Line 2. Line 2 runs south toward the Bell Tower and South Gate; Line 4 is often more direct for Xi'an Station, Daming Palace or the Yanta area. Use the live map to choose the station and exit closest to the hotel entrance; follow station signs when a lift is needed. Recheck service after collecting baggage and reaching the concourse. A scheduled landing time is not a safe basis for the last train.

p.src: Xi'an North is large. The useful question after the gates is not whether south or north looks quicker, but which mode comes next. Lines 2, 4 and 14 meet here; the north and south plazas have their own public-transport areas, and taxis and ride-hailing use designated zones. Start with the hotel direction, then account for luggage and the people travelling with you. Follow line signs for the metro. For a car, follow the current exit signs to the correct pickup level rather than chasing one map pin through the building.

p.src: Xi'an Station is the rail hub outside Jiefang Gate on the north side of the wall; it is not Xi'an North. After expansion, the station has south, north and underground access, with Metro Line 4 connected. The durable orientation is easier than memorising exit numbers: the wall lies south and Daming Palace National Heritage Park north. On arrival, identify the side you have used, then follow signs for the old city or Line 4. On the ticket, the word North identifies a different station.

p.src: Xi'an East opened on 30 June 2026, so an old guide or offline map may omit it. The official opening report says passengers can follow signs to Metro Line 5 within a five-minute walk, while buses, taxis and ride-hailing occupy separate transfer zones. This is still a new hub: update the map before travel, verify that the ticket says Xi'an East in China Railway 12306, and read the day's exit and pickup signs on arrival. Circulation at a new station may change, so follow the signs on site.

p.src: Use the metro for the longest cross-city leg when luggage is manageable and service is still running. A bus works for the last section only when the live map makes the stop name, direction and alighting point clear; if the stop and map disagree, return to rail or use a car. With heavy luggage, tired companions, a night arrival or a hotel entrance still far from the station, go directly to the signed taxi or ride-hailing zone. Save walking for the final section after both exit and entrance are known.

p.src: Rail stations and the metro involve security checks. Keep identity documents, ticket details, power banks and items likely to need separate inspection near the top of the bag. Hold a wheeled case on the platform and gather the group before gates or escalators. Turn toward a lift as soon as its sign appears instead of reaching a staircase with the case. If wheelchair, guidance or boarding assistance is needed, request China Railway 12306 priority-passenger service in advance and confirm every segment. Check current official rules for restricted items and service eligibility before departure.

p.src: Airport (T5) station currently supports single tickets, cash, transport cards and QR options, with equipment for foreign bank cards. That does not mean one payment method will work on every overseas phone or at every station. If the travel QR will not open, buy a single ticket at the machine or service centre instead of troubleshooting at the gate. Keep the hotel's Chinese name, full address, entrance pin and phone number available offline. For a car, send the entrance rather than only the hotel brand.

p.src: For a night arrival, use the time when you have the bags and are outside the gates, not the scheduled landing or train arrival. Include walking, security, ticket purchase and transfer. If that leaves too little time for an unhurried rail transfer, switch to the signed taxi or ride-hailing pickup zone. Before entering the car, match the vehicle to the booking, send the hotel's Chinese address and entrance, and keep the group together. Do not turn the final leg into a race merely to preserve the original route.

p.src: Check only six things: the exact station on the ticket, the flight terminal, the actual arrival time, today's status of the next service, the hotel's Chinese address and entrance, and the station exit or signed pickup zone. Check once before departure and again after landing or leaving the train. If a change is needed, adjust the next leg first; do not immediately change hotels or rebuild the whole day. Once the hub, entrance and pickup point are unambiguous, the remaining route is clear.
